strings.name: Kazuyo Sejima
strings.role: Architect · Transparency, flow and shared space
strings.summary: Sejima studied architecture at Japan Women’s University and worked with Toyo Ito before establishing her own practice and co-founding SANAA with Ryue Nishizawa. The 21st Century Museum in Kanazawa, New Museum in New York and Louvre-Lens reorganize cultural space through light materials, multiple routes and open boundaries. She also independently designs houses and university facilities. A joint Pritzker laureate in 2010, she continues examining relationships between buildings, environments and users.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1956–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Explored transparency, flowing space and scale through SANAA's cultural and public buildings, influencing spatial expression in contemporary architecture.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Multiple routes through cultural space
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Designed with Ryue Nishizawa, Kanazawa’s circular museum uses separate galleries and multiple entrances to connect exhibition routes with everyday city life.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Lightness and shared environments
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: SANAA uses transparent boundaries, soft daylight and continuous spaces in projects such as Louvre-Lens to reconsider relationships between art, landscape and the public.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses architecture and environment in India
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Following a New Delhi lecture, she spoke at CEPT University in Ahmedabad about shared space, daylight and nonhierarchical layouts, emphasizing how users’ activities shape architecture.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: SANAA receives the Royal Gold Medal
strings.timeline.event-02.text: RIBA awarded the medal to Sejima and Nishizawa’s collaborative practice, recognizing its sustained exploration of inclusion, accessibility and relationships with the environment.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Sydney Modern opens
strings.timeline.event-03.text: SANAA’s new building for the Art Gallery of New South Wales expanded public art facilities through layered galleries, outdoor spaces and connections to the landscape.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Louvre-Lens opens
strings.timeline.event-04.text: With Nishizawa, low volumes, glass and aluminum respond to the former mining area’s terrain and connect the museum with its surrounding landscape.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Pritzker recognition and Venice direction
strings.timeline.event-05.text: She shared the Pritzker Prize with Nishizawa and directed the twelfth Venice architecture exhibition, exploring relationships between people and architectural space.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: New Museum opens in New York
strings.timeline.event-06.text: SANAA stacked and shifted box-like volumes to create galleries, terraces and public facilities in Manhattan’s Bowery neighborhood.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Kanazawa’s 21st Century Museum opens
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Designed with Nishizawa, the circular cultural building uses separate galleries, transparent exterior walls and multiple entrances to explore an open civic museum.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Co-founds SANAA with Ryue Nishizawa
strings.timeline.event-08.text: The architects formed a collaborative team while maintaining their independent offices, developing a shared practice in housing, cultural and public buildings.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Establishes her own architectural office
strings.timeline.event-09.text: After working at Toyo Ito’s practice, she established Kazuyo Sejima & Associates in Tokyo and developed her spatial language through independent projects.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Completes graduate architectural studies
strings.timeline.event-10.text: She completed graduate study at Japan Women’s University and joined Toyo Ito’s office, moving from academic training into architectural practice.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Ibaraki Prefecture
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Ibaraki, she later studied architecture in Tokyo and developed a career combining independent design with collaborative practice.
